headline: Tishomingo County School Board Covers Staffing, Technology, and Athletics
summary: The board approved personnel, field trips, donations, two student transfers, revisions to 14 district policies, a revised payroll schedule and a 25-cent increase in student breakfast and lunch prices. It also approved software subscriptions, insurance renewals and service agreements, and scheduled the annual public budget hearing for July 21 and a special called budget meeting for July 30.
publicComment: No one appeared for public comments.

personnel.note: Hires include a substitute teacher, a summer worker at $10/hour, 3 bus drivers (one half-route), coaching assignments, teachers and a high school assistant principal at Belmont School; other = 1 revised teacher contract; 1 employee transfer.

money.item: Grant for Tishomingo Middle School students attending the National FBLA competition (accepted)

policy.item: Approved revisions to 14 district policies, including attendance, student conduct, school wellness, artificial intelligence, employee compensation, retired teacher employment, promotion and retention, Title I family engagement, purchasing and procurement, and school calendar requirements.
Changed the payroll schedule: January payroll moved up one week, reducing the holiday gap between pay periods from six weeks to five.
Increased full-paid student lunch from $3.25 to $3.50 and breakfast from $2.00 to $2.25; adult prices rise to $4.50 lunch and $2.75 breakfast.
Discussed whether to adopt a policy for forming student clubs and an approval process for graduation stoles and cords; no action taken.

superintendent: Superintendent Christie Holly reported that a new state attendance law limits excused absences, requires attendance plans for students over the limit and raises minimum attendance from 63% to 66% of the school day.
Holly reported that districts with chronic absenteeism above 10% must implement attendance improvement plans, with Mississippi Department of Education guidance expected by Aug. 15.
Holly also updated the board on changes to employee payroll procedures and increases in meal prices.
